Action Plan:
1. Acute diarrhea: advise soft, easily digestible diet (e.g., crackers, toast, jam, mashed/boiled vegetables) for at least 48 h after last loose stool before re-introducing meat, eggs, fish, or dairy (except yoghurt).  
2. Hydration: encourage liberal oral fluids and begin oral re-hydration salts (Dioralyte, OTC) after each loose stool.  
3. Probiotics: yoghurt permitted to help restore gut flora.  
4. Red-flag education: seek medical review immediately if stools ≥ 6–8/day, signs of dehydration, blood or mucus in stool, high or persistent fever, or if diarrhea lasts > 7 days.  
5. Contingency plan: arrange stool culture if symptoms persist beyond 1 week or if blood appears; attend ED if unable to maintain hydration.  
6. Follow-up: contact clinic via app or schedule review if above red flags occur or no improvement in 7 days.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for consult: 3-day history of diarrhea.  
• History of present illness:  
  – Onset 3 days ago; no recent travel or suspicious food intake.  
  – Frequency 4–5 loose/watery stools/day; variable consistency.  
  – Associated symptoms: mild abdominal pain, single episode of emesis, mild fever (subjective), decreased appetite.  
  – Denies blood or mucus in stool.  
  – Continues adequate oral intake; no overt dehydration.  
• Past medical history: asthma.  
• Family history (relevant): father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer at 62 y.  
• Medications: “Laxepro” inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: none reported.  
• Social history: not discussed.

Objective:
• Video assessment: patient appears well hydrated; no other physical examination documented.  
• No vitals or labs provided.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral or self-limiting bacterial)
   – Differential: food-borne bacterial enteritis, inflammatory bowel disease flare (less likely), medication-induced diarrhea.
   – Investigations planned: none at present; stool culture if symptoms > 7 days or blood/mucus develops.
   – Treatment planned: dietary modification (soft diet), oral re-hydration salts, yoghurt/probiotics, maintain fluid intake.
   – Referral: ED if dehydration or ↑ stool frequency; none otherwise.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: vital signs, complete medication list with correct drug name/dose, social history (smoking, alcohol), immunization status.  
● Internal conflicts: uncertainty regarding name of asthma inhaler (“Laxepro”); actual agent unverified.  
● Transcript quality: clear; occasional overlaps and minor inaudible sections but clinically adequate.
